text: What is the largest ocean on Earth by surface area?
explanation: The Pacific Ocean covers about 46% of Earth's water surface and is larger than all of Earth's land area combined.

text: The $\textbf{Eiffel Tower}$ is a landmark located in which European capital city?
explanation: Located on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France, it is one of the most recognizable structures in the world.

text: Which country has the most natural $\textbf{lakes}$ in the world?
explanation: Canada has more lakes than the rest of the world's countries combined.

text: What is the capital city of $\textbf{Japan}$?
explanation: Tokyo is the political and economic center of Japan and the seat of the Emperor.

text: Which river carries the largest volume of water in the world?
explanation: The Amazon River in South America discharges more water than the next seven largest rivers combined.

text: The $\textbf{Galápagos Islands}$, famous for their biodiversity, belong to which country?
explanation: This archipelago is located in the Pacific Ocean, about 906 km west of continental Ecuador.

text: Which European country is known as the $\textbf{Land of Fire and Ice}$ due to its volcanoes and glaciers?
explanation: Iceland is geologically active with many volcanoes, yet also has massive glaciers like Vatnajökull.

text: What is the capital city of $\textbf{China}$?
explanation: Beijing has been the capital of China for centuries and is known for the Forbidden City.

text: The $\textbf{Suez Canal}$ connects the Mediterranean Sea to the:
explanation: Located in Egypt, it provides the shortest maritime route between Europe and the lands lying around the Indian and western Pacific oceans.

text: Which continent is the $\textbf{coldest, driest, and windiest}$ on Earth?
explanation: Antarctica is almost entirely covered by ice and holds the record for the lowest temperature ever recorded on Earth.

text: What is the deepest lake in the world?
explanation: Located in Siberia, Russia, Lake Baikal is the deepest and oldest freshwater lake in the world.

text: Which country is home to the $\textbf{Acropolis}$ of Athens?
explanation: The Acropolis is an ancient citadel located on a rocky outcrop above the city of Athens.

text: The $\textbf{English Channel}$ separates the United Kingdom from which country?
explanation: At its narrowest point, the Strait of Dover, the distance is only about 34 kilometers (21 miles).

text: What is the capital city of $\textbf{Egypt}$?
explanation: Cairo is the largest city in the Arab world and is located near the Nile Delta.

text: Which mountain range stretches across Italy from north to south?
explanation: The Apennines form the backbone of the Italian peninsula.

text: Which country possesses the territory of $\textbf{Greenland}$?
explanation: Greenland is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.

text: The $\textbf{Mississippi River}$ empties into which body of water?
explanation: It flows south through the central United States to the Gulf of Mexico.

text: What is the capital of $\textbf{Germany}$?
explanation: Berlin was reinstated as the capital of Germany following the reunification in 1990.

text: Which country is known as the $\textbf{Land of a Thousand Lakes}$?
explanation: Finland actually has over 180,000 lakes.

text: The $\textbf{Strait of Malacca}$ is a major shipping lane located between Malaysia and which Indonesian island?
explanation: It is one of the most important shipping channels in the world.

text: Which South American country is long and narrow, stretching along the Pacific coast?
explanation: Chile averages only 177 km wide but is over 4,200 km long.

text: What is the capital of $\textbf{Russia}$?
explanation: Moscow is the political, economic, and cultural center of Russia.

text: The $\textbf{Alps}$ mountain range does NOT pass through which of these countries?
explanation: The Alps are in Central Europe; Spain is separated from France by the Pyrenees.

text: Which country is located on the $\textbf{Anatolian Peninsula}$?
explanation: Anatolia, also known as Asia Minor, makes up the majority of modern-day Turkey.

text: What is the largest $\textbf{desert}$ in the world (including polar deserts)?
explanation: A desert is defined by precipitation, and Antarctica is the largest area with very low precipitation.

text: Which city is famous for its $\textbf{Golden Gate Bridge}$?
explanation: The bridge spans the Golden Gate strait, the one-mile-wide channel connecting San Francisco Bay and the Pacific Ocean.

text: What is the capital of $\textbf{Spain}$?
explanation: Madrid is located in the center of the Iberian Peninsula.

text: Which is the highest capital city in the world?
explanation: La Paz, Bolivia, sits at an elevation of roughly 3,650 meters (11,975 ft) above sea level.

text: The $\textbf{Caspian Sea}$ is traditionally classified as the world's largest:
explanation: Although called a sea due to its size and salinity, it is technically an endorheic basin (lake).

text: Which country has $\textbf{three}$ capital cities (Pretoria, Cape Town, Bloemfontein)?
explanation: Pretoria is the executive capital, Cape Town the legislative, and Bloemfontein the judicial.

text: The $\textbf{Seine River}$ flows through which major city?
explanation: The Seine divides Paris into the Left Bank and the Right Bank.

text: Which U.S. state is the largest by $\textbf{land area}$?
explanation: Alaska is more than twice the size of Texas, the next largest state.

text: What is the capital of $\textbf{New Zealand}$?
explanation: Wellington is the southernmost capital of a sovereign state in the world.

text: Which island nation is located off the southeast coast of $\textbf{India}$?
explanation: Sri Lanka is separated from India by the Palk Strait.

text: The $\textbf{Rocky Mountains}$ are a major mountain range in:
explanation: The Rockies stretch some 3,000 miles from British Columbia in Canada to New Mexico in the US.

text: Which country is the world's largest producer of $\textbf{coffee}$?
explanation: Brazil has been the world's largest coffee producer for over 150 years.

text: What is the capital of $\textbf{Argentina}$?
explanation: Buenos Aires is located on the western shore of the Rio de la Plata estuary.

text: The $\textbf{Pyrenees}$ mountains form a natural border between France and which country?
explanation: The Pyrenees stretch from the Bay of Biscay to the Mediterranean Sea.

text: Which Asian country was formerly known as $\textbf{Siam}$?
explanation: The country officially changed its name to Thailand in 1939.

text: What is the capital of $\textbf{Italy}$?
explanation: Rome is known as the 'Eternal City' and has been the capital since the unification of Italy.
